column1: # Kalay interiors: refugees from Gondowan, trade families, shops, inns, Colosso party, and Mind Read.

column3:
I came to spread goodwill,
but Kalay's people seem to
have learned that from{page_break}Hammet already. There's
much I could learn here.{end_wait}

Lunpa's family used to help
the poor, even if they were
thieves. Now I hear his{page_break}grandson is terrorizing
people.{end_wait}

Lunpa stole from the
wealthy and helped people
who had nothing. His son{page_break}Donpa followed him. Dodonpa
seems to have forgotten
why.{end_wait}
The road north of Vault\nused to be safe. These days\nI wouldn't travel it alone.{end_wait}
Lunpa once had a good name.\nDodonpa has done a fine job\nruining it.{end_wait}
Everyone talks about the\nnorth now. Three years ago,\nno one here gave it a{page_break}thought.{end_wait}

A merchant from Vault was
warning people about the
north. Then the soldiers{page_break}brought him to Hammet's
palace.{end_wait}
Three years ago, strangers\nraided Mt. Aleph. Since\nthen, trouble keeps coming{page_break}from the north.{end_wait}
Everyone says the northern\nroads are dangerous. We\nused to think Kalay was{page_break}beyond all that.{end_wait}

The bridge to Vault is
fixed, but we still aren't
allowed through. That{page_break}doesn't sound like a road
repair problem to me.{end_wait}

My son thinks I'm too
strict. He hasn't seen what
the roads are like now.{page_break}Lady Layana is right to be
careful.{end_wait}
I'm old enough to work and\nearn money. I should be old\nenough to choose where I{page_break}travel.{end_wait}
Let him call me unfair. I'd\nrather have an angry son\nthan no son at all.{end_wait}
A good merchant knows a\nfine blade from a poor one\nbefore he sets a price.{end_wait}
My son learned to bargain\nfrom Lord Hammet. Now he\ntries it on me at supper.{end_wait}

Never cheat a customer.
Hammet taught me that.
People remember who treated{page_break}them fairly, and they come
back.{end_wait}
My son counts every coin.\nEven when I ask him to buy\ndinner, he wants to know{page_break}what he'll get in return.{end_wait}
Are you going to Tolbi too?{end_now}
Everyone at the inn is\ntalking about Colosso.\nIt'll be strange when they{page_break}all leave.{end_wait}
I've paid for the Tolbi\ntour. I've been saving all\nyear. Now I can barely keep{page_break}still.{end_wait}
Have you seen the Colosso\nfighters? Those men are\nbuilt like walls.{end_wait}
If you're on the tour,\nfinish eating. We can't\nkeep the whole group here{page_break}for one last bite.{end_wait}
Tolbi has markets, inns,\nand fine sights. I wish\npeople talked about those{page_break}as much as Colosso.{end_wait}
Lord Hammet loves Colosso.\nI wonder if he'll make it\nto Tolbi this year.{end_wait}
I might have entered\nColosso when I was younger.\nThese knees would make a{page_break}poor showing now.{end_wait}
Another group heading to\nTolbi? That festival keeps\nour rooms full.{end_wait}
You look like fighters. I\nbet you've thought about\nentering Colosso at least{page_break}once.{end_wait}
Do you know much about the\ncontinent south of Tolbi?{end_now}
We leave for Tolbi shortly.\nI've checked my bags twice,\nand I've still forgotten{page_break}something.{end_wait}
We fled Gondowan and left\nLalivero behind. I never\nimagined we'd have to go so{page_break}far to feel safe.{end_wait}
Lalivero is bigger than\nmost towns on Gondowan.\nKalay is busy enough, but I{page_break}still miss home.{end_wait}
Thinking of entering\nColosso? Too bad for you.\nBoth of us are competing{page_break}this year.{end_wait}
Ouranos and I will reach\nthe finals. Then we'll\nsettle which of us is{page_break}stronger.{end_wait}

A clever merchant sells
more than goods. Look at
this tour. People are{page_break}paying just to travel
together.{end_wait}
Every year the whole town\nruns off to Tolbi. Someone\nhas to stay and keep the{page_break}shops open.{end_wait}
I paid for the tour because\nI don't know the roads. Let\nsomeone else worry about{page_break}where to sleep.{end_wait}
I've been guessing who'll\nwin Colosso all week. I\nnever pick the right{page_break}fighter.{end_wait}
Most of these tourists\naren't used to walking all\nday. I'll be glad when{page_break}we're aboard the ship.{end_wait}

I've counted the tickets,
packed the bags, and
answered the same questions{page_break}all morning. I need a
holiday myself.{end_wait}
This is my first Colosso. I\nwas so excited I barely\nslept. Don't tell the{page_break}others.{end_wait}
The moment I see a fight, I\nwant to jump in. My wife\nsays that's why she won't{page_break}let me enter.{end_wait}
All this fuss over men\nwrestling and swinging\nswords. There are better{page_break}ways to spend a day.{end_wait}
I'm entering Colosso as\nsoon as I reach Tolbi. I'll\nworry about the other{page_break}fighters when I see them.{end_wait}
People have come here from\nGondowan, far to the south.\nI wonder what the journey{page_break}cost them.{end_wait}
I've never seen Tolbi\nbefore. Everyone keeps\ntelling me how grand it is.{page_break}I hope they're right.{end_wait}
I can speak my mind here\nwithout being punished. I\ndidn't think that would{page_break}ever feel ordinary.{end_wait}

Colosso starts soon, and
everyone is rushing off. I
can't see why a festival{page_break}calls for this much
trouble.{end_wait}
I'm stronger than Sean, and\nhe's faster than me. We'll\nsee which matters more in{page_break}Colosso.{end_wait}
Nobody trains as hard as we\ndo. You can tell the other\nfighters that.{end_wait}
The tour group is gone. I\nnever thought I'd miss the\nnoise, but this inn feels{page_break}empty now.{end_wait}

Even our chef went to
Colosso. There's hardly
anyone left to feed, but I{page_break}still have to keep the inn
running.{end_wait}
Wait, wasn't he with the\ntour? He's going to be\nfurious when he realizes{page_break}they left without him.{end_wait}

We came here to get away
from trouble in the south.
Now everyone is leaving{page_break}town for a festival. I
don't understand it.{end_wait}
We fled the northeast of\nGondowan. It's quiet here\nnow. I can finally hear{page_break}myself think.{end_wait}
If I'd known trade would be\nthis slow, I'd have joined\nthe tour. At least I'd have{page_break}seen Tolbi.{end_wait}
My husband would spend\nevery coin in Tolbi if I\nlet him. Someone has to{page_break}keep him sensible.{end_wait}
I wanted the inn to be\npeaceful. Now it's so quiet\nI keep listening for{page_break}voices.{end_wait}
Everyone talks about\nColosso. I didn't leave\nLalivero and cross the sea{page_break}to chase a festival.{end_wait}
The trip from Lalivero\nfrightened me. Kalay still\nfeels strange, but I can{page_break}finally sleep without fear.{end_wait}
